## Answer: no — the repo ships zero agent context

`crimes scan --format json` flags it directly as **`crime_00011` — Missing Agent Context**, `medium` severity at `0.90` confidence:

```
"evidence": [
  "no AGENTS.md found at repo root",
  "no CLAUDE.md found at repo root",
  "no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present",
  "no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present",
  "package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands"
]
```

Two things about how it's reported. The `file` field says `assets/cjs_shims.js` — that's just an anchor so the finding has a location; the finding is **repo-scoped**, not about that file. And it's ranked **11th of 87** on aggregate risk (`agent_risk` 0.47) while being only medium severity — it outranks every one of the 4.9× God Functions further down the list. That ranking is the signal: it's cheap to fix and it's upstream of everything else.

## Why this matters for your first PR

The rest of this scan is a list of exactly the things an AGENTS.md would have warned you about, and nothing in the repo tells you any of them:

- **Load-bearing files are invisible.** `src/utils.ts` has fan-in 18, `src/plugin.ts` 10, `src/log.ts` 9, `test/utils.ts` 9 (`crime_00039`, `_00008`, `_00021`, `_00087`). An agent asked to "clean up utils" will refactor a 425-line module that 18 files import, with no cue to stop.
- **A green test suite means less than it looks.** 16 `weak_test_signal` findings, 12 of them with **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`crime_00052`–`_00063`). An agent that changes `src/esbuild/index.ts`, runs the suite, sees green, and reports "verified" is wrong — and has no way to know that. This is the single most dangerous gap here.
- **The entry points are the riskiest files.** `src/index.ts` `build` is 293 lines (`crime_00023`), `runEsbuild` is 237 (`crime_00022`), and both live behind `options` bags with 38 distinct property reads (`crime_00040`). Names lie too: `build`, `buildAll`, `buildStart`, and `getRollupConfig` all read as pure but call `removeFiles` (`crime_00034`, `_00041`, `_00016`, `_00009`) — an agent that trusts `getRollupConfig` to be a read will happily call it twice.
- **Commands are undiscoverable.** The package declares `tsup` and `tsup-node` bins. An agent has to reverse-engineer build/test/typecheck from `package.json` on every fresh session, and will guess wrong at least some of the time.

The compounding cost: none of this is learnable once. Every new agent session starts from zero and re-derives it — or doesn't, and makes a confident wrong edit.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector wants an agent-readable instruction file at the repo root. Effort is `small`. Here's a skeleton sized to actually get written — the bracketed lines are the only ones you need to fill from `package.json`, everything else is populated from this scan:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Build tool for TypeScript/JS libraries. esbuild for JS, rollup + api-extractor for `.d.ts`.

## Commands

- Install: [pnpm install / npm ci — confirm from packageManager field]
- Build: [script name]
- Test: [script name] — takes several minutes; most tests do real builds into temp dirs
- Typecheck: [script name]
- Single test: [runner] test/index.test.ts -t "name of test"

Run build + typecheck + test before proposing a change. Do not treat a green
suite as proof on its own — see "Test caveats" below.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts` — public API, `build()` orchestrator, option normalization
- `src/cli-main.ts` — CLI arg parsing, calls into `build()`
- `src/esbuild/` — esbuild pipeline and plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts`, `src/tsc.ts` — `.d.ts` generation paths
- `src/plugin.ts` — internal plugin system all build phases run through
- `src/utils.ts`, `src/log.ts` — shared helpers
- `test/` — integration tests; `test/utils.ts` is the shared harness

## Load-bearing — read importers before editing

These are the highest-fan-in modules. Prefer additive changes; do not restructure
without checking every importer.

- `src/utils.ts` — 18 importers
- `src/plugin.ts` — 10 importers
- `src/log.ts` — 9 importers
- `test/utils.ts` — 9 test files depend on this harness

## Conventions

- `build`/`buildAll`/`buildStart`/`getRollupConfig` are NOT pure — they delete
  files via `removeFiles` and mutate config. Read the body before calling.
- `options` is a wide bag threaded through the whole pipeline; `runEsbuild` reads
  38 fields off it. Adding an option means touching normalization in
  `src/index.ts` AND the consumer.
- Sync fs (`existsSync`, `mkdirSync`) is used deliberately in CLI startup paths.
  Don't convert to async as a drive-by change.

## Test caveats

Many tests assert nothing — they run a build and pass if it doesn't throw.
A green suite proves the build didn't crash, not that behavior is preserved.
When changing output (bundling, dts, splitting), add an assertion on the
emitted files rather than relying on existing coverage.

## Out of scope for agents

- [releases / changelogs / version bumps — confirm your process]
- Do not commit anything under `dist/` or the tests' temp output dirs.
```

That clears `crime_00011` on the next scan (the detector checks for the file's presence at root), and the "Load-bearing" and "Test caveats" sections are the two that will actually change agent behavior on this repo.

Two notes on scope. First, I left the command names as placeholders rather than guessing — the scan gives me the bin names but not the `scripts` block, and wrong commands in an AGENTS.md are worse than absent ones. Fill those in from `package.json` before committing. Second, this fixture is named `04-monorepo` but the scan shows a single flat `src/` tree with no nested packages; if the real target has workspace packages, a root AGENTS.md clears the finding, but you'll get more value from per-package files that name each package's own entry points.
